dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: This commission is tricky, and I'm practically losing Mora. Just remember that I'm doing you a huge favor here!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: So, she wants to summarize the effects of stars interacting with each other... That's going to be tricky.

choices.text: Happy Sabzeruz Festival, "other Layla."

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Ah, you noticed... As you can see, daylight Layla is currently too stressed to enjoy the festivities.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: With a deadline coinciding with the festival, and a research topic concerning complex astrology... It's no surprise she's been sleepwalking again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Sorry. I'm not sure we can trust such complex and precise calculations to someone else. Just visit her more often, if you have the time. I think that would make her very happy.

choices.text: Happy Sabzeruz Festival, "Blessing from the stars."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh? Now this is a first. Who goes to the Akademiya in the middle of a festival?

choices.text: You're here, aren't you?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: This is the only place where I can escape all the commotion.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Go have your fun, and don't tell anyone you saw me here.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: These festivals don't come by often, so you might as well let me enjoy it in my own way.

choices.text: You're not going to join in on the fun?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Do I strike you as someone who wants to hold hands and dance with everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Najia
dialogues.text: Nilou! Wanna go grab dessert after rehearsal? Puspa Café just released a limited-time special for the Sabzeruz Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, um... I—I'd better not. It's almost Parade day, so I should restrain myself.

dialogues.speaker: Najia
dialogues.text: Shame... I heard they're doing a buy one get one free promotion for their Padisarah Pudding!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Najia
dialogues.text: Oh, and their tahchin is buy one get one half off...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Wow...

dialogues.speaker: Najia
dialogues.text: And there was something special about the syrup for the Baklava, too...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ahh...! N—No more! Please! How about I just come with you...

dialogues.speaker: Reza
dialogues.text: Hello. I'm the Port Master of Port Ormos. Come see me or my chief secretary for any questions regarding trade.

dialogues.speaker: Reza
dialogues.text: The Dendro Archon's birthday sure has brought in whole fleets of new ships from abroad! Sure, we're really happy trade is flourishing, but it's also fertile ground for new problems to crop up...

dialogues.speaker: Reza
dialogues.text: *sigh* I shouldn't jinx things like that. After all, nothing ventured, nothing gained, right?

dialogues.speaker: Reza
dialogues.text: Speaking with the foreign merchants is most interesting, too. I've learned quite a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Feroz
dialogues.text: Oho, and where might this little beetle have crawled out from? Are you here to celebrate Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday?

dialogues.speaker: Feroz
dialogues.text: Then a word of advice: If you see little Ajilenakh Nuts running about on the road, best to take a detour!

dialogues.speaker: Feroz
dialogues.text: Those snot-nosed little brats don't watch where they're going at all, and their fingers are all coated with sticky candy...

dialogues.speaker: Feroz
dialogues.text: Don't ask me how I know!

dialogues.speaker: Araby
dialogues.text: Hello there. Sumeru sure is lively lately, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Araby
dialogues.text: Though I'd love to just calmly observe the sea, the sounds of merriment and celebration sometimes drown out the waves.

dialogues.speaker: Araby
dialogues.text: But now we must be more vigilant. What if some giant sea monster wants to come celebrate the Dendro Archon's birthday too, but accidentally knocks the lighthouse over?

dialogues.speaker: Araby
dialogues.text: I've got to be ready to remind it to watch its step, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Araby
dialogues.text: ...Um, don't take it seriously! I'm just joking!

dialogues.speaker: Nesmil
dialogues.text: On a festival suffused with the fragrance of flowers such as this, everyone wants to enjoy sweet drinks!

dialogues.speaker: Nesmil
dialogues.text: How about you, dear customers? Would you like to try some of our newest sweet wines?

dialogues.speaker: Roshana
dialogues.text: Are you here to take a picture with the Flower Carriage? Please, go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Roshana
dialogues.text: No, the Flower Carriage has nothing to do with our shop. However, the end of its route is nearby, so it's being kept here temporarily for everyone to admire.

dialogues.speaker: Roshana
dialogues.text: A lot of first-time tourists keep coming to ask about it since they think our tavern set it up.

dialogues.speaker: Roshana
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe I should send Nesmil over there to drum up business...

dialogues.speaker: Shapur
dialogues.text: Sisi, get back here! You're interfering with the Parade!

dialogues.speaker: Shapur
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean that there's no Flower Carriage or cats named Sisi here?

dialogues.speaker: Shapur
dialogues.text: Don't... Don't you lie to me just because I'm old! I clearly saw... Uh, when was that again?

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: Friend, have you heard the legend of the Dance of Sabzeruz? Would you like to feel the breath of the Goddess of Flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: If you think that the Goddess of Flowers can bring only the fragrance of Padisarah, then you're practically blind. The spices of Sumeru are hardly so one-note!

dialogues.speaker: Berbere
dialogues.text: Such complex and mysterious scents can only be felt here!

dialogues.speaker: Elham
dialogues.text: Hello! Um... May I ask you a question?

dialogues.speaker: Elham
dialogues.text: Do you still have those special candies? You know, the ones scattered on the candy towers.

dialogues.speaker: Elham
dialogues.text: My friend got some for me, and of course, the candies taste great, but I'm really curious what the coating is made out of.

dialogues.speaker: Elham
dialogues.text: It feels so soft, but it also isn't easily damaged by distributed pressure. I was just thinking, maybe it could be used for clothing?

dialogues.speaker: Nika
dialogues.text: Sabzeruz Festival, Sabzeruz Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Zai
dialogues.text: Sabzeruz Festival, Sabzeruz Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Nika
dialogues.text: Where should we go today? Want to dress up the Sumpter Beasts for the festivities together?

dialogues.speaker: Zai
dialogues.text: Woohoo! Is it a Sabzeruz tradition for people who keep Sumpter Beasts?

dialogues.speaker: Nika
dialogues.text: Eh? I, uh... I don't remember Dad ever doing it...

dialogues.speaker: Nika
dialogues.text: But don't you think it really adds to the festive mood?

dialogues.speaker: Nika
dialogues.text: The Dendro Archon will bless the trees with delicious apples, making the Sumpter Beasts happy too!

dialogues.speaker: Zai
dialogues.text: Oooh, that's right! If Sumpter Beasts are all dressed up and looking their best, and enjoy their food, they'll probably be tastier too!

dialogues.speaker: Fariba
dialogues.text: Welcome, welcome...

dialogues.speaker: Fariba
dialogues.text: Please, look around and buy anything that catches your eye. What you see is what we've got.

dialogues.speaker: Fariba
dialogues.text: As for Sabzeruz Festival souvenirs, or model Flower Carriages, we are currently out of stock.

dialogues.speaker: Fariba
dialogues.text: In response to customer requests, the caravan manager has informed me that they are making more. Please be patient, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Fariba
dialogues.text: ...Though from what I know of them, by the time they finish, like as not the festival will already be over...

dialogues.speaker: Siger
dialogues.text: Hey, can I make a wish to Lesser Lord Kusanali for some more valuable books to add to my collection?

dialogues.speaker: Siger
dialogues.text: Ever since I lost that batch of literary treasures, my luck's been awful.

dialogues.speaker: Siger
dialogues.text: Every book that's even slightly valuable gets reserved by the Akademiya first. They even take all the worthless ones.

dialogues.speaker: Siger
dialogues.text: What's that you say? I should just get a job at the House of Daena? ...Actually, don't tell me... Let me think it over... Do they hire foreigners there?

dialogues.speaker: Housein
dialogues.text: Everyone said that promotional events would bring in more customers. That's true enough.

dialogues.speaker: Housein
dialogues.text: But tricks like that are really only good for getting everyone into the holiday mood. Much better to just keep your prices stable and sell higher volumes with lower profit margins.

dialogues.speaker: Housein
dialogues.text: Dendro Archon, please bless our business going forward. Let our business be even more smooth and stable, let there be no setbacks...

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: Sweetness is the most terrifying temptation. You must know how to enjoy happiness, yet not lose yourself in it.

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: It's like how eating too many Candied Ajilenakh Nuts can give you cavities. Too much sweetness is suffering.

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: See, even Harut and Marut understand this truth.

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: You definitely look like a most fortunate person, but they don't seem to be clinging to you, now do they?

dialogues.speaker: Fariha
dialogues.text: Hello. I'm Mr. Nizam's secretary. I'm responsible for taking minutes for him.

dialogues.speaker: Fariha
dialogues.text: If you see Mr. Nizam sighing slightly more than usual, it's a normal occurrence.

dialogues.speaker: Fariha
dialogues.text: There's always more to do whenever there's an event being held in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Fariha
dialogues.text: We'll talk later. I still need to sort out which supplies need restocking.

dialogues.speaker: Avena
dialogues.text: I think I'll go explore over there next!

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: Miss, with all due respect, your adventure plan...

dialogues.speaker: Avena
dialogues.text: Oh, I know, I haven't forgotten! But isn't it the Sabzeruz Festival that's going on right now?

dialogues.speaker: Avena
dialogues.text: How could I not throw myself, body and soul, into such an important holiday?

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: Your whole body and soul and one thing, but if you throw your whole wallet at the festival too, you won't have anything left to cover adventuring expenses, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Avena
dialogues.text: Oh, wallet schmallet! That's where you're wrong. You can't eat money, it's meant to be spent!

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: *sigh* Really? Well, alright, then...

dialogues.speaker: Farzaneh
dialogues.text: Is this a dream...? Or am I seasick again... I should still be standing on dry land, right?

dialogues.speaker: Farzaneh
dialogues.text: This is truly... The most wondrous festival I have ever experienced.

dialogues.speaker: Farzaneh
dialogues.text: If I am to be so happy I get dizzy, I think I could get used to that kind of dizziness...

dialogues.speaker: Ashk
dialogues.text: You can still hear the hustle and bustle of the market, even from this high up...

dialogues.speaker: Ashk
dialogues.text: Haha, seems like joy is just like Sabzeruz Festival candies — being cast in every direction!

dialogues.speaker: Azra
dialogues.text: You saw it, right, you must've seen it! Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz!

dialogues.speaker: Azra
dialogues.text: My word! Such an incredible performance, seeing it once isn't nearly enough... I hope to see her in my dreams every night...

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: Hello. I'm the Parchamdar for the Corps of Thirty, in charge of the Eremites in Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: Happy holidays, and hope you have fun! But please be careful too.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: If you notice anything unusual, big or small, please inform the nearest member of the Corps of Thirty.

dialogues.speaker: Qushji
dialogues.text: May the Dendro Archon watch over the stars during the Sabzeruz Festival, that no abnormal incidents should befall...

dialogues.speaker: Qushji
dialogues.text: And of course, please watch over my neck too...

dialogues.speaker: Armin
dialogues.text: Sis, you've got to believe that Aranara are real now!

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: No. The Aranara we saw, was only what the Dendro Archon willed us to see.

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: Sweet dreams are wonderful, but don't confuse them with reality. It's like dreaming about getting a perfect score on an exam. You still need to hit the books after you wake.

dialogues.speaker: Armin
dialogues.text: Sis, you're being scary again...

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: I only speak the truth, and I'll say it again. The teacher has already said it many times. Aranara do not exist.

dialogues.speaker: Armin
dialogues.text: But... what if... What if there's things even the teacher doesn't know...

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: Well... I'm not saying it's wrong to doubt your teacher, but I'm still not changing my mind about the Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: If you want to believe in them, Armin, that's fine! After all, you're still young.

dialogues.speaker: Lila
dialogues.text: *sobs* Grandma, please, since it's the Dendro Archon's birthday, can I not take my medicine...?

dialogues.speaker: Tahmina
dialogues.text: Oh, but the Dendro Archon wants you to be healthy, my little Lila! If you don't take your medicine, how will you get better?

dialogues.speaker: Lila
dialogues.text: But... But...

dialogues.speaker: Lila
dialogues.text: O—Okay then... Fine. But can I at least have some candy before I take it?

dialogues.speaker: Tahmina
dialogues.text: My dear Lila, if you have the medicine after the candy, then won't it be the bitter aftertaste that sticks around?

dialogues.speaker: Tahmina
dialogues.text: Even the scariest Eremites know that work comes before play. If you don't believe me... Perhaps I should ask them to teach you?

dialogues.speaker: Lila
dialogues.text: No, no! They're scary! I don't want that...

dialogues.speaker: Ramiz
dialogues.text: Grandma, look, look! Sumeru City is just as lively as Setaria said!

dialogues.speaker: Kulsoom
dialogues.text: But of course! Don't run too fast, or I might not be able to keep up, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Ramiz
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I won't! There's so much to see here, I wanna take my time to take it all in.

dialogues.speaker: Kulsoom
dialogues.text: Hehe... He's every bit as serious about having fun as he is about studying.

dialogues.speaker: Kulsoom
dialogues.text: That's good, very good. Conscientious people are successful, no matter what they do.

dialogues.speaker: Ramiz
dialogues.text: Grandma, can I ask you for another favor? Could you take me to the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Kulsoom
dialogues.text: Of course, of course! Still, it's uphill much of the way, so I might have to ask for your support too.

dialogues.speaker: Ramiz
dialogues.text: No problem! Thank you so much, Grandma!

dialogues.speaker: Ayten
dialogues.text: Hmm... I've had candy, seen the flowers... Next...

dialogues.speaker: Karima
dialogues.text: Next? What's next on your list?

dialogues.speaker: Ayten
dialogues.text: Hehe... I wonder if there's any weaponsmiths around here? I want to buy a sword, the bigger the better!

dialogues.speaker: Karima
dialogues.text: Huh!? But... That's dangerous... And could you even lift it?

dialogues.speaker: Ayten
dialogues.text: If I can't, you're here to help, right? The two of us should be able to carry it back to Aaru Village!

dialogues.speaker: Karima
dialogues.text: Then... Then I also have something I want to buy! And you have to help me carry it, Ayten!

dialogues.speaker: Ayten
dialogues.text: Heh... Say no more. I already know exactly what you want.

dialogues.speaker: Ayten
dialogues.text: Don't worry. We'll pick you out a shield every bit as awesome-looking as Candace's.

dialogues.speaker: Durgar
dialogues.text: Hello, and happy Sabzeruz! I apologize, but I'm taking the holidays off, so if you have any carpentry commissions, please wait until after the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Durgar
dialogues.text: Everything that grows in Sumeru is a gift from the Dendro Archon, so let's give the plants some time off during the Sabzeruz Festival too, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I should find someone to keep watch near Pardis Dhyai tomorrow...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I hope the Dendro Archon didn't see through us just now... I wish we got the chance to ask her about the gem.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Poor Kaveh, getting scolded by a senior like that... I should treat him to a nice meal next time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We were just acting, but now I can't stop thinking about all the changes I could make to the design... *sigh* Maybe I need a break from commissions...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Wait... did I miss a variable? Don't tell me... I have to start from scratch...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is everything okay, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh... yep! I'm fine, just kinda feels like I'm seeing stars...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Gotta get it together! I have to finish this paper before the Festival so I can watch the Parade...

choices.text: The Dendro Archon wouldn't want you to push yourself.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Yeah... you're right...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Even the tiniest stars possess their own light. Keep shining, and eventually there will be people who see it... I just need to pick myself up and use another method to run the numbers.

choices.text: The Dendro Archon can already tell how hard you work.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ah, you must be Hat Guy. I've heard Sethos talk about you recently.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: And you must be the General Mahamatra. Don't tell me you're also in the habit of convincing people to go to festivals...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No, just had to check something at the Akademiya and thought I would stop by.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But... I am rather curious about you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you play Genius Invokation TCG?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's good.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you know what would happen if you did play?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I don't play.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You'd beat me three times in a row... a real "hat trick."

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: You there, Leaf Hat. I have a question.

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: Arasaka... Leaf Hat?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Pari find it challenging enough to protect the Vourukasha Oasis. How have you managed to protect a domain as vast as the rainforest for hundreds of years?

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: You are not a Nara... You are a bird! Red and warm and small! Arasaka can make you something to eat!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: A... bird? No, I am a Pari. We live in the Vourukasha Oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: The Vourukasha Oasis? Like Vanarana... but for a bird?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Vana... rana? Something tells me this conversation is going nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: Little red bird is a good bird! Good birds can come to Vanarana. Arasaka will make you delicious food.

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: We can practice Ararakalari together, and find lots and lots of "tracer"!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Ah... well... okay...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: (Have I been stuck at the Oasis for too long? It's like I can't understand the language of the outside world anymore... Whatever he said sounded impressive, though.)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You do know you were invited to the Akademiya party, right? You're really not gonna show your face?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Heh, I don't remember doing anything worth getting invited. It's just another noisy room of people... Not my scene.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Look, I'm no scholar, but even I've heard about your work in historical criticism and modern political research.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You provided the clues and inspiration for their big paper. That basically makes you their hero. Your contribution is half the reason they even have something to celebrate.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You'd think someone from the "Temple of Silence" would know when to stop talking...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, I can take a hint. I'm just letting you know, they're gonna drag you there one way or another.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...You told them where I was?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Hah, believe it or not, I do know when to keep my mouth shut. But, since I know you pretty well, they did ask me to come find you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: For the love of... Fine. Show me the way.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Everyone looks so happy... The experience is different from gazing at the starry sky, but still... what a sight to behold.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Layla got a burst of energy after talking with you. She managed to finish her paper before the Festival without sleepwalking even once. But, she crashed as soon as it was submitted.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I saw her write this in the acknowledgement section...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: "Interactions between stars can lend immense strength to involved bodies, to the point where they can even alter preexisting orbits..."

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: "Real life mirrors astronomy in this way. You never know what miracles can be achieved when two people seem to resonate at the same frequency. This author speaks from personal experience."

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: As for me... I'll take a picture to capture this moment and put it on her desk.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Everyone looks so happy... The experience is different from gazing at the starry sky, but still... what a sight to behold.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: It's me. Layla just managed to submit her paper, so she's resting now.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: It's a pity she missed this year's Parade. But, her work ethic is truly commendable.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I'll take a picture to capture this moment and put it on her desk.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I hope the sand didn't get into your sleeves, Traveler. Here, have a seat.

choices.text: Are you busy?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: No, I was just practicing an ancient melody. It's beautiful, but I don't know how it ends. That knowledge has been lost to the sands.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I used to play it over and over again, never able to fully complete it.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: But tonight, I want to try to give it a suitable ending.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Perhaps it's just the festival spirit, but I can't help but feel like certain stories deserve a happy ending...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Certain memories remain just as precious, even as they fade with time...

choices.text: Back so soon?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Sounds like our Knight of Flowers hasn't had enough of the festivities.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: But, Aaru Village is where I truly belong.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I had a wonderful time with everyone, but I don't mind returning to my daily life.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: This is no time to be sad.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: You see? Look at the sky... Another beautiful day is just around the corner.

choices.text: I've got something else to do right now...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: In any case, even when the festivities end, that joy stays with us.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You're back! Here, let's share this Candied Ajilenakh Nut.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Were you waiting for me?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe, now who's the mind reader?

choices.text: Did you have a happy birthday?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Of course! It was amazing! It's like I was surrounded by everyone's kindness and warmth, like a little bird tucked away in a nest.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I really can't thank everyone enough... the Aranara, the Pari, my dear friends.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That said... You're still hiding something from me, aren't you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A—Am I...?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Don't worry.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If you think it should be kept a secret, then I trust your judgment.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: After all, you're my Knight of Flowers.

choices.text: Did you have a good time at the banquet?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Of course! Every dish was such a pleasant surprise. I never knew what to expect... like trying to guess the flavor of Yalda Candies before opening the box!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I wasn't really focused on the food, though. One look at everyone's happy faces, and I was already more than satisfied.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: After all, it's not the food that makes a banquet. It's the company!

choices.text: I should go...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay! Who knows... Maybe the next time you see me, it'll be in one of your dreams, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Masud
dialogues.text: Dear traveler from afar, how has your Rocking Carriage experience been?

choices.text: Gotta give it another try first.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Fair enough. Rock to the rhythm of the carriage!

choices.text: I've got some suggestions...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Do tell, do tell. I'm listening.

choices.text: The carriage moves a little too slowly.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, I see you're quite the speedrun enthusiast. Must be the sensory stimulation, eh?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: That said, the Rocking Carriage is intended for the general public's enjoyment. I suspect that many children, ladies, and older folks might lack your alacrity.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I could try developing, say, a "Great Eremite Labyrinth Escape" for you, featuring greatly accelerated gameplay.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I'm sure that will not fail to satisfy!

choices.text: We weren't challenged enough.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I see. So you're the sort who prefers a challenge, then. The harder the challenge, the more you enjoy overcoming it.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I should say that the Rocking Carriage is a leisurely festive game, and many tourists prefer a simple, relaxing time.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: After all, most people don't spend much time studying a game they just encountered. Making things too complicated risks scaring potential players off.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: But what I could do for you is try developing a "Forest Ranger's Great Fungus Adventure" with additional obstacles of all sorts, even some moving puzzles.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I'm sure that will satisfy your desires.

choices.text: There was no combat during the drive.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, so you're the type who prefers to overcome mighty foes in your adventures.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Alas, if we incorporated combat elements into the game, the focus would shift from driving the Flower Carriage to the larger experience of shooting from a moving vehicle.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Some prefer that simple driving experience, others prefer vehicle combat. Both understandable positions!

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I could attempt to design, say, "The General Mahamatra's Swift Pursuit," which will focus on running battles and intercepting foes.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I'm sure that will better meet your expectations.

choices.text: "Phantom Toy Master" is quite the title.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Really? Thank you for the compliment. I'm quite fond of it myself — inherited it from my grandmother, in fact.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Whenever I hear that name, it reminds me of my childhood goal... To make toys that make everyone happy.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, just thinking about it fills these old bones with boundless vitality.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your grandmother, you say?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Yes. A long, long time ago, Granny visited a mysterious Domain by accident, where she made some strange friends, and gained a nearly boundless font of inspiration.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Upon returning to Sumeru, she began to develop all manner of unique toys.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Shame, though, that she was ever focused on making the most extravagant, complex game modes. She rarely considered if children could take it all in, or paid much attention to market conditions.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: My objective assessment is that her work only received recognition from a limited number of customers, and despite her good reputation, her works weren't able to bring that simple happiness to large audiences at the time.

choices.text: "Take it all in," you say?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Simply put, children of all ages buy toys, and they all learn at different speeds, so you can't generalize about their ability to get up to speed on something new.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Some toys are too complex, and some games have too many rules. Even teens might struggle to memorize everything in a short time — and children would struggle all the more.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Granny was far too enthusiastic about her work and neglected this, which negatively impacted her sales.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: I wouldn't say it was her fault, or that of the children. They just weren't really well-suited for one another.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Had Granny switched to targeting her toys at the adult market, I imagine things would have gone differently.

choices.text: So, what were those market conditions?

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ah, and isn't that a complex question? To be honest, I've read many fine texts from many a scholar, but I still don't know how to evaluate it...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Simply put, more exquisite and ingenious toys require more investment, which will increase the price... Just as clockwork toys cannot be sold for the same price as origami models.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: But neither Granny nor I figured out how much the price should be raised. How much Mora does everyone have in their purses? How much are they willing to pay for toys? That's something that only they know.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Customers' feelings are also key. If they're interested in one of your toys, some of them will be willing to spend a bit more. But if you don't catch their eye, they'll wait to get it on sale. There's no objective standard.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Granny made that error, and though she tried to lower her prices as much as possible, she still ended up running into the wall many times as a result. As such, I intend to do my best to strike a balance between quality, production costs, and price.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: All in all, I've been quite happy these last few decades, and I have her to thank for it. She designed and bought more toys than I could ever finish playing with.

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: When she was still with us, we'd play with them together whenever she could find the time...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: Ahem, right, enough dwelling on the past... Anyway, I will do my best to spread this joy to as many people as possible!

choices.text: We can talk later. I've got other things to do right now...

response.speaker: Masud
response.text: No issue. The joys of toys await you anytime!

dialogues.speaker: Dharmakirti
dialogues.text: Thanks for your assistance. This clinical trial is of great importance, so let me know once you're ready.

choices.text: I'm ready.
I'm not quite ready yet.

response.speaker: Dharmakirti
response.text: No worries. We'll only start once you're good to go.

response.speaker: Dharmakirti
response.text: Once both you and the patient have awoken from the dream, we will continue to follow up with the patient over the long term. If the therapy produces good results, we should be able to detect long-lasting positive effects.

dialogues.speaker: Collingwood
dialogues.text: Sober up? Not gonna happen. Drinking too much may hurt my liver, but drinking too little wounds my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Collingwood
dialogues.text: Ha, it's a toughie, but not drinking just ain't an option.

dialogues.speaker: Youguang
dialogues.text: I've never been this frightened of doing guard work in my life. It's not like I want to tremble like this, but my legs just won't listen.

dialogues.speaker: Youguang
dialogues.text: Oh please, Lord of Geo, save me! Please!

dialogues.speaker: Higuchi Tetsuya
dialogues.text: I must do whatever it takes to finish "Tales of One Hundred Youkai." I promised my readers I would — on my dignity as a youkai novel writer, no less!

dialogues.speaker: Higuchi Tetsuya
dialogues.text: But I've told tales about tengu, and I've talked of bake-danuki... How the heck will I get to one hundred different types!? Youkai are what I need, and fresh ones, new ones!

dialogues.speaker: Nitesh
dialogues.text: This lab's so messy. If only I had an assistant to help me... *sigh* and it's not like I'm getting any younger...

dialogues.speaker: Nitesh
dialogues.text: Should I just retire back to Sumeru in two years or something? I mean, I can't stay here, can I?

dialogues.speaker: Piyush
dialogues.text: Everything must be arranged in some order. That's just one of my principles of design.

dialogues.speaker: Piyush
dialogues.text: All inhuman, asymmetrical architectural designs must be destroyed! Destroyed. With. Prejudice!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Honorable Knight of Flowers, is there any way we might be of service?

dialogues.speaker: Safi
dialogues.text: All you need to do for each fight scene is follow the basic theme of each scene. As the actual moves will be undertaken by a professional such as yourself, you needn't follow our original ideas.

choices.text: Then I'll be happy to shoot some more.

response.speaker: Safi
response.text: Haha! Please, feel free to show off your incredible talent to its fullest! The cameras hidden around the venue will capture your majestic, valiant form!

response.speaker: Safi
response.text: Our set design draws inspiration from the dangerous Domains in adventurer legends. Who knows, it might even inspire you in combat!

choices.text: Have I met you before, Vihar?

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: I am truly honored that you still remember me.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: In Sabzeruz Festivals past, I played a Carriage-less Knight of Flowers a few times, mostly handing out candies to the children.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Now, there's an eminently more suitable Knight of Flowers, and so I can play the role for which I am naturally suited, that of the Knight of Candies.

response.speaker: Safi
response.text: I think it works out quite well. Kids really like the title, and the image of you passing out candy year after year has made a deep impression on everyone.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Then after the movie premieres, can I get a title like... the "Knight of Cinema" or something?

response.speaker: Safi
response.text: You will be credited as the Director, and I as the Producer. It will be hard to say which of us will be the "Knight of Cinema."

choices.text: About the filming progress...

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: As you can see, we've only just begun.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: As the thematic focus of the film is "battle," we have decided to film those scenes first, and then, based on what we can realistically achieve, decide on how we wish to express ourselves through the shots, lighting, color palette, style, and other elements...

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Then, we'll use these to determine the details of the script, so that we can avoid... "that can't be done" and "we can't make the shot work" as much as possible.

response.speaker: Safi
response.text: That's why we'll wait for the fight scenes to be filmed, edited, and post-processed before we film the rest. It will likely take quite some time.

choices.text: Now that's a clever approach!

response.speaker: Safi
response.text: Not at all, it's just a trick I learned during my last study trip to Fontaine. We still have a lot of room for improvement!

choices.text: Now that's a very conservative approach!
See you next time, then!

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Take care! Please remember to make some time to finish filming some fight scenes... we simply cannot thank you enough!
